newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan inflation up 2.17 pct in January.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan inflation up 2.17 pct in January.

text.p: Pakistan's monthly inflation rate jumped more than two percent in January, figures released on Tuesday showed, underlining a key challenge facing prime minister-elect Nawaz Sharif.
The consumer price index rose 2.17 percent in January compared with December, the Federal Bureau of Statistics said.
That represented a year-on-year increase of 13.4 percent, up from 11.41 percent in December and 8.93 percent in January 1996.
Raza Mirza, head of research at brokerage house Khadim Ali Shah Bukhari and Co Ltd, said fuel price increases seemed to be behind the rise.
"Fuel prices seem to be the main driving force, although food has gone up as well," he said.
Fuel prices rose mainly because of higher international prices, Mirza said. Pakistan has linked domestic fuel prices to international levels since June 1996.
Gas charges went up 26.5 percent in January and kerosene 4.75 percent.
The wholesale price index also surged 2.3 percent in January over December. It rose 15.74 percent in January year-on-year, compared with 14.41 percent in December.
"The more worrying factor is that the wholesale prices are also moving up at a slightly faster pace," Mirza said.
He said Sharif's new government, due to be sworn in next week, would have to work hard to curb price rises to avoid any knock-on impact on the value of the rupee.
Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League easily won general elections on February 3.

Pakistan's caretaker government promised to bring the inflation rate down to 11 percent for the whole of the 1996/97 (July-June) financial year as part of conditions for a standby loan from the International Monetary Fund.
